description: Questions extracted from this AI Atlas conversation; wording is labeled per case. Evidence references were checked in the preceding topic research, November 1, 2026. Candidate answers require human review.

cases.question: How does my local coding workflow compare with this browser/cloud workflow?
cases.originalExcerpt: im used to the workflow of vibe coding on local host with claude code them publishing it to github and making a pull request to merge, then publishing to github pages
cases.origin: Local/cloud topic request in this conversation
cases.proposedAnswer: The development workbench moves from your computer to a remote workspace. Both can edit, test, preview, push a feature branch, review a pull request, merge, and deploy through GitHub Actions to Pages. A remote AI model can assist either workbench.
criteria: Shows where files, terminal, tests, and preview run in each workflow.
Shows the shared branch → PR → merge → Actions → Pages path.
Distinguishes assistant model location from workspace location.

cases.question: Does cloud coding need setup again on every edit, making local iterations faster?
cases.originalExcerpt: right now you have to set everything up again but if its local vibe coding its much faster per iteration due to no need to setup cost
cases.origin: Local/cloud topic request in this conversation
cases.proposedAnswer: A configured local project often reaches the first edit faster than a fresh cloud workspace. A warm cloud workspace can reuse tools and dependencies too. Startup, model waiting, build time, compute and network latency should be measured separately; one cold start does not establish every-edit performance.
criteria: Separates startup time from edit-to-preview time.
Explains reuse in a warm cloud workspace.
Avoids claiming local is always faster or cloud always rebuilds.
Acknowledges that new local environments also need setup.

cases.question: What happens when the cloud workspace sleeps, and does the live website stop?
cases.originalExcerpt: everything on cloud (and earlier today the cloud was sleeping)
cases.origin: Local/cloud topic request in this conversation
cases.proposedAnswer: Sleep or stopping may preserve files while processes need restarting; deletion or replacement can require reconstruction. The exact retention rules depend on the service. GitHub Pages serves the deployed website independently of the development workspace.
criteria: Separates sleep/resume from deletion/rebuild.
Does not assume Codespaces policies apply to Codex.
Explains why the published site can remain available while development sleeps.

cases.question: What are the practical pros and cons of local and cloud coding?
cases.originalExcerpt: so i can see the differences and the pros and cons
cases.origin: Local/cloud topic request in this conversation
cases.proposedAnswer: Local offers a familiar, reusable setup and no remote-terminal round trip, with hardware and maintenance constraints. Cloud can offer access from multiple devices, isolation, consistent images and remote compute, with startup, network, cost and retention trade-offs. Neither location by itself guarantees speed or reproducibility.
criteria: Compares startup, iteration, continuity, access, cost and data flow.
Includes drawbacks and useful scenarios for both.
Explains that hosted AI calls may transmit context even from a local workbench.

cases.question: What mental model helps me understand AI cloud deployment?
cases.originalExcerpt: if there's a better mental model to think through this help me format as well
cases.origin: Local/cloud topic request in this conversation
cases.proposedAnswer: Start with workbench → repository → live site. Then ask three independent questions: where do I build, where does the app run, and where does inference run? A locally developed app can be cloud-hosted. An AI app using a secret API key generally needs a backend to protect it; static Pages hosting alone does not supply that backend.
criteria: Separates development, repository review, production hosting and inference.
Explains that local development can publish to cloud hosting.
Identifies that today’s Atlas is static and makes no runtime model calls.

cases.question: Can agents read shared repository instructions before starting work?
cases.originalExcerpt: create an md file in the repo because im using multiple agents to vibe code and they can read the instructions before they start work on the repo
cases.origin: Agent instructions and eval question-bank request in this conversation
cases.proposedAnswer: The root AGENTS.md documents architecture, commands, source verification, collaboration, question-bank rules and the PR/deployment workflow. Compatible coding agents can discover it; other tools may need to be explicitly pointed to it. Reading a file is a convention, not an enforcement mechanism.
criteria: Root AGENTS.md exists and is linked from README.
Instructions describe actual commands and files.
Protects concurrent work and defines a handoff.
Does not claim every agent automatically reads or obeys it.

cases.question: Can I review my questions and judge whether the answers are correct as an eval?
cases.originalExcerpt: a question bank of my questions in a separate page so i can verify if my questions were answered correctly as part of 'evals'
cases.origin: Agent instructions and eval question-bank request in this conversation
cases.proposedAnswer: Each case preserves a user-question excerpt alongside a clearly labeled paraphrase, a proposed answer, acceptance criteria, evidence, and an answer link. You decide Pass or Needs work and record why. Reviews are saved in this browser and can be exported; they are not automatic factual verification or shared agent state.
criteria: Includes traceable user questions, not invented prompts.
Shows expected criteria and evidence separately from the candidate answer.
Defaults to Not reviewed and requires a human verdict.
Persists verdicts and notes, supports export, and flags older case revisions.
